passage: My name is Ojas and I am in Blue House. On Sports Day I cheered only when the Blue relay team ran. When Red House won the skipping race, the others in Blue said, "They cheated!" and I shouted it too, even though I had not watched. Nirmala from Red House looked at me and said, "I skipped my best." I felt hot in the face. I said I did not mean her. Later I saw her sitting alone with her medal, and I thought, she is not a Red. She is Nirmala.

qa.q: Why did Ojas shout "They cheated!" without having watched the race?
qa.a: Ojas felt the excitement of belonging to Blue and joined the others' cheering, so the rival side became a little less human; the hot face afterwards shows embarrassment.

qa.q: What could Ojas do to soften the rivalry after the race?
qa.a: Ojas could go to Nirmala and say well done, since one kind word shows that the other house is made of real people.

qa.q: How might Nirmala have felt when hearing "They cheated!" from the Blue House?
qa.a: Nirmala probably felt hurt and proud at once, having done her best; saying "I skipped my best" shows she wanted the true story to be known.

grounding: A child cheers only for their own house and downplays rivals, finding belonging exciting while the other side becomes a little less human.

passage: Note from Shankar Sir after the inter-section quiz. Lakshmi's section, 6B, lost to 6C by two points, and Lakshmi led the booing every time 6C answered. When a 6C child hesitated, six children in 6B whispered, "Wrong! Wrong!" and Lakshmi said, "They always cheat." Nobody in 6B stopped it, though two children looked uneasy. Afterwards I asked the class to name one thing 6C had got right. Lakshmi went quiet, then said, "Their answer about rivers." I plan a mixed-section quiz next week. — Shankar Sir

qa.q: By how many points did 6B lose to 6C?
qa.a: Section 6B lost to 6C by two points.

qa.q: Why did Lakshmi say "They always cheat" about 6C?
qa.a: Lakshmi felt the sting of losing and the pull of belonging to 6B, so blaming the other side felt easier than admitting the loss; the feeling was rivalry mixed with disappointment.

qa.q: What did Shankar Sir do that could soften the rivalry?
qa.a: Shankar Sir asked the class to name something 6C got right and planned a mixed-section quiz, so children work with the other section rather than against it.

qa.q: What might the two uneasy children in 6B have been feeling?
qa.a: They probably felt uncomfortable at the whispering but did not want to break from the group, so they stayed silent.

grounding: A child cheers only for their own section and downplays rivals, with belonging making the other side seem less human.
